facts.statement: Dollosuchus is an extinct genus containing only one species of tomistomine crocodilian.
facts.quote: Dollosuchus (meaning "Louis Dollo's crocodile") is an extinct monospecific genus of tomistomine crocodilian

facts.statement: Dollosuchus possessed large openings above its eyes, a feature also seen in Kentisuchus and Thecachampsa.
facts.quote: It had large supratemporal fenestrae in relation to its orbits, similar to Kentisuchus and Thecachampsa.

facts.statement: The genus was first described using many jaw fragments discovered in the Early to Middle Eocene Bracklesham Beds Formation in the UK.
facts.quote: Dollosuchus was originally described on the basis of numerous mandibular fragments found from the Early to Middle Eocene Bracklesham Beds Formation in the United Kingdom.

facts.statement: A nearly complete skeleton found in Belgium in 1915 was originally described by Swinton in 1937 as Dollosuchus but later became the basis for the separate taxon Dollosuchoides densmorei.
facts.quote: A nearly complete skeleton from Belgium (IRScNB 482) discovered in 1915 and described by Swinton in 1937, and referred to Dollosuchus, formed the basis of the new taxon Dollosuchoides densmorei.

facts.statement: Dollosuchus is considered the oldest known tomistomine crocodilian based on recent phylogenetic analyses.
facts.quote: It is a basal form possibly related to Kentisuchus, according to several phylogenetic analyses that have been conducted in recent years, and is the oldest known tomistomine to date.

facts.statement: Fossils of Dollosuchus have been discovered in Belgium and the United Kingdom.
facts.quote: Fossils have been found from Belgium and the United Kingdom.

facts.statement: It is no longer likely that Charactosuchus kugleri is a synonym of Dollosuchus because it is now classified in the family Crocodylidae.
facts.quote: Charactosuchus kugleri, another Eocene crocodilian, has been suggested to be synonymous with Dollosuchus, but this is no longer likely because C. kugleri is now thought to be a member of the family Crocodylidae

facts.statement: Researchers have suggested that Kentisuchus spenceri, Megadontosuchus arduini, and Dollosuchus dixoni might belong to the same genus.
facts.quote: It has been suggested that Kentisuchus spenceri, Megadontosuchus arduini, and Dollosuchus dixoni are cogeneric.

facts.statement: The original material used to describe Dollosuchus cannot be distinguished from other related long-snouted crocodilians.
facts.quote: The material cannot be distinguished from other related longirostrine, or long-snouted, crocodilians.

rejected.statement: Recent phylogenetic analyses suggest Dollosuchus is a basal form possibly related to Kentisuchus.
rejected.quote: It is a basal form possibly related to Kentisuchus, according to several phylogenetic analyses that have been conducted in recent years
